rules.quote: The optional Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI) can be used to implement non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor. The Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI) can be used to implement non-branching instructions in external cores:
rules.condition: implementing non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor
rules.statement: The PCPI can be used to implement non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor core.

rules.quote: When an unsupported instruction is encountered and the PCPI feature is activated (see ENABLE_PCPI above), then pcpi_valid is asserted, the instruction word itself is output on pcpi_insn, the rs1 and rs2 fields are decoded and the values in those registers are output on pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2.
rules.condition: an unsupported instruction is encountered and PCPI is activated (ENABLE_PCPI)
rules.statement: The core asserts pcpi_valid, outputs the instruction word on pcpi_insn, and outputs the rs1 and rs2 register values on pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2.

rules.quote: An external PCPI core can then decode the instruction, execute it, and assert pcpi_ready when execution of the instruction is finished.
rules.statement: An external PCPI core can decode and execute the instruction and assert pcpi_ready when execution is finished.

rules.quote: Optionally a result value can be written to pcpi_rd and pcpi_wr asserted.
rules.statement: The PCPI core can optionally write a result value to pcpi_rd and assert pcpi_wr.

rules.quote: The PicoRV32 core will then decode the rd field of the instruction and write the value from pcpi_rd to the respective register.
rules.condition: PCPI core returns a result with pcpi_wr asserted
rules.statement: The PicoRV32 core decodes the rd field of the instruction and writes the pcpi_rd value to the respective register.

rules.quote: When no external PCPI core acknowledges the instruction within 16 clock cycles, then an illegal instruction exception is raised and the respective interrupt handler is called.
rules.condition: no external PCPI core acknowledges the instruction within 16 clock cycles
rules.statement: An illegal instruction exception is raised and the respective interrupt handler is called.

rules.quote: A PCPI core that needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction, should assert pcpi_wait as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts pcpi_ready.
rules.condition: the PCPI core needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction
rules.statement: The PCPI core should assert pcpi_wait as soon as the instruction is decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts pcpi_ready.

rules.quote: This will prevent the PicoRV32 core from raising an illegal instruction exception.
rules.condition: pcpi_wait is asserted by the PCPI core
rules.statement: Asserting pcpi_wait prevents the PicoRV32 core from raising an illegal instruction exception.
